newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: U.S. tells Argentina patent law hurts investment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tells Argentina patent law hurts investment.

text.p: A senior aide to U.S. President Bill Clinton urged Argentina Wednesday to update patent laws that are a sticking point in its relations with Washington, and which he said get in the way of investment.

White House Senior Counselor Thomas McLarty, speaking in Buenos Aires before meeting President Carlos Menem, said the United States was "frankly disappointed" by a law passed this year which only phases in patent protection over five years.

Patents have been a point of discord in the otherwise cozy relationship between Argentina and the United States in the past two years. Washington says foreign pharmaceutical firms lose $500 million a year in Argentina to bootleggers, while Argentine drug firms have lobbied Congress successfully.

"While we realize this is an important issue for pharmaceutical companies in Argentina, we believe the current situation will inhibit investments. It is important for the Argentine consumer and the health of the whole industry," the Clinton aide told a news conference.
McLarty was on a tour of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay -- partners with Paraguay in the new Mercosur customs bloc.
He rejected talk of Mercosur, which includes Chile as an associate, would impair the formation of a Western Hemisphere-wide free trade area.

"I do not believe the entrance of Mercosur and intra-regional growth it has experienced is detrimental to the achieving of the Free Trade Area of the Americas by the year 2005," he said, adding that such trade blocs were only healthy as long as they promoted free trade "not only among member countries but also among non-member countries."
McLarty said the recently reelected U.S. president was keen to visit the region having "heard wonderful reports from his wife Hillary". But he said it was to early to set a date.
